setting_and_country.value: School of Nursing and Midwifery, Monash University, Australia
setting_and_country.quote: This study was conducted at a single School of Nursing and Midwifery at an Australian university.

design.value: Mixed methods exploratory sequential: post-retreat online evaluation (content analysis) and publication outcomes (descriptive statistics)
design.quote: The design was a mixed methods exploratory sequential design consisting of two distinct phases and data collection methods.

participants.value: 112 attendees over six retreats: 94 academics and 18 research students (4 Honours, 2 Masters, 12 PhD); 70 evaluation respondents
participants.quote: Over the six writing retreats a total of 112 participants attended: 94 academics from Assistant Lecturer to Professor level and 18 research students from Honours to PhD level.

group_format.value: Semi-structured retreats twice a year, three days and two nights, 14 h of dedicated writing in 2–3 h blocks, opt-in research training and expert peer feedback
group_format.quote: Each writing retreat offered 14 h of dedicated writing time in blocks of 2–3 h across the three-days.

comparison.quote: In phase two, quantitative data, including the number and quality of publications arising from each writing retreat were collected

confidence_self_efficacy.value: NR (confidence named as an aim; not measured)
confidence_self_efficacy.quote: help demystify the process and grow their confidence

other_writing_outcomes.value: 81 planned publications: 60 published (74%), 5 under review, 5 not submitted, 11 abandoned; 43 of 60 in Q1–Q2 journals; PhD candidates published 12 manuscripts
other_writing_outcomes.quote: Of these, 60 had been published (74%), 5 were under review (6%), 5 had not yet been submitted (6%), and 11 were abandoned (13%).

notes: Research students are 18 of 112 participants; their experience is not reported separately. Five of the 11 abandoned papers came from Masters or PhD research.
